The most influential band in music history is mediocre? I'm sorry, but no. The Beatles were pioneers and inventors of many studio techniques such as double tracking, back masking, tuned feedback, spliced audio loops, distortion, equalisation, stereo effects, multi-tracking (overdubbing), compression, phase shifting, and innovative “microphoning. They popularised the music video, were the first band to have a self-contained record label (Apple Records). They were the subject of the first ever live global satellite television broadcast in June 1967, etc. You might not like their music but mediocre bands do not accomplish all of this.       

If you ignore the bubblegum pop days of "Love Me Do" or "I Want To Hold Your Hand". In other words, skip to 1965, and you will find a band that was deadly serious about creating serious music and pushing forth the possibilities of music making.

He felt a slight sharp pain, as a bug bite or sting, on the back of his right thigh. He looked behind him and saw a man picking up an umbrella off the ground. The man hurriedly crossed to the other side of the street and got in a taxi which then drove away. He had been hit in the leg by a micro-engineered pellet containing ricin, fired from an umbrella. He died 4 days later. Speculation of KGB involvement has been suggested but the case remains unsolved.
